Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Singhadurbar, Nepal, on November 5, 2026. Photo: X/@PM_nepal_.

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the expected upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.

Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.

Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.

The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.

Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.

stories.title: Iranian officials welcome U.S. midterm results after voters rebuke Trump administration, Iran war
stories.content:
Pictures of U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are seen on a dartboard in Tehran on Wednesday, during the 47th anniversary of the U.S. expulsion from Iran. (Majid Asgaripour/WANA/Reuters) Social Sharing Iranian officials on Wednesday celebrated U.S. voters' rebuke of the Republican Party and President Donald Trump in the midterm elections, as the region waited to see how the results could affect the Iran war.

Concerns about the war's effects, particularly frustration over rising prices for fuel and other goods in the U.S., helped Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's vote.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, wrote on X. "If the U.S. [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a nightmare."

The broader region has been on edge over the prospect of the U.S. resuming full-scale military operations against Iran for the first time in almost two months. Talks aimed at preventing renewed fighting continue, while other U.S. allies in the region are urging Washington against resuming full-scale operations in the war, now more than eight months old, which has rattled the global economy and devastated Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly pushed for more strikes, while Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal.

U.S. midterms: How Trump, Vance and Canadian politicians responded the day after Democrats' massive gains

Despite ceasefire agreements and repeated diplomatic efforts, military confrontations have continued in southern Iran and around the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about a return to full-scale fighting.

Iran's supreme leader said those who think partisan changes in the United States can change its enmity toward the Islamic Republic are "gravely mistaken."

In a letter shared on his social media account, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who hasn't been seen publicly since the war began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Feb. 28, said: "If there are still those who harbour even a slight hope for a change in behaviour or partisan and factional shifts within the system of domination, or who imagine that by giving concessions to America they can dissuade it from hostility toward the Iranian nation, they are gravely mistaken."

stories.title: Delhi's toxic winter air is back - is the Indian capital prepared for pollution?
stories.dek: The Delhi government has announced a four-month winter action plan, but experts say that won't be enough.
stories.content:
Image source, Reuters Image caption, People exercise in a park in Delhi on Thursday, breathing in hazy, polluted air

There are two cardboard boxes in Meenu Rana's living room in Delhi. One is filled with Diwali decorations and twinkling lights. The other holds air purifiers.

"The mornings have already started feeling stuffy. It will get worse in the coming days, so it's better to be prepared," says the 43-year-old teacher.

She is not alone. Every year, as winter and the festive season approach, residents of India's capital begin preparing for something far less celebratory: months of breathing polluted air.

Delhi and its satellite cities record some of the world's highest pollution levels through the year. But as winter sets in, the air often becomes unbearable.

Falling temperatures and slower winds trap pollutants close to the ground instead of allowing them to disperse. Smoke from crop residue burning in neighbouring states adds to emissions from vehicles and factories, as well as construction dust. Firecrackers used during festivals often worsen air quality.

The result is noxious air and a familiar question: why does pollution return year after year, and why hasn't more been done to tackle it?

This year, however, the Delhi government announced its Winter Action Plan months before the worst of the smog arrived. The plan is in place from 1 November to 28 February, covering the months when pollution usually spikes.

Experts have called this a step in the right direction, noting that in previous years measures were often rolled out only after the air quality got too bad to ignore. However, they say this by itself won't be enough, calling for more holistic, long-lasting measures.

Just days after the plan came into effect, the city is slipping back into a depressingly familiar pattern .

This week, a grey haze hangs over Delhi, along with a distinct smoky smell that residents unwillingly recognise. People complain of irritation in their eyes and difficulty breathing, and coughs and sneezes are heard everywhere.

For those who can afford them, air purifiers have become a household necessity. Outdoors, people wear masks or cover their faces with cloth, trying to protect themselves from the worst of the pollution.

stories.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
stories.dek: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents.
stories.content:
Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.

Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.

Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup’s new always-on “Teammates” can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.

Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer , an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates “build on top” of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete “ongoing, large-scale work.” You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously — much like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet . Perplexity’s take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan.

Perplexity notes that you can keep tabs on Teammates’ progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack. “Over time, we envision every org having hundreds of teammates working for each person,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says on X .

stories.title: A clever molecular trick unlocks previously impossible properties in glass
stories.dek: Scientists have discovered how to reprogram the internal structure of glass using a special molecule that rearranges chemical bonds while lowering the melting temperature.
stories.content:
Scientists have developed a new way to change the internal structure of glass while it is being made, giving them greater control over properties such as magnetism and the way the material interacts with light. The discovery could open the door to advanced glasses with capabilities that were previously difficult or impossible to achieve.

The breakthrough comes from a collaboration involving TU Dortmund University, Paderborn University, the University of Duisburg-Essen, and the University of Oxford. Published in Nature Materials , the research demonstrates how adding a particular organic molecule during the melting process can rearrange chemical bonds within certain types of glass.

The method also allows these materials to melt at much lower temperatures, preventing the damage that would otherwise occur during manufacturing. Such specialized glasses have potential applications in gas storage, batteries, optical technologies, and catalysis.

"We have found a way to chemically modify the structure of glasses derived from so-called metal-organic framework compounds - or MOFs for short - right during the manufacturing process," explains Prof. Dr. Sebastian Henke from TU Dortmund University, who led the study.

The key ingredient is a molecule called 1,10-phenanthroline. When introduced during production, it performs two important tasks. It reduces the temperature needed to melt the material while also changing how metal atoms connect with surrounding molecules.

This combination allows researchers to create glass with magnetic or light-emitting characteristics that previously could not be achieved without exposing the material to potentially destructive temperatures.

To understand why this approach matters, it helps to consider how glass normally forms. When a liquid cools quickly enough, its atoms become locked into a disordered arrangement rather than forming the repeating pattern found in crystals.

"Normally, glass is formed when a molten liquid cools rapidly. The solid structure then sets without the atoms arranging themselves in a regular pattern. Until now, researchers often had to accept the chemistry of these glasses as dictated by the starting material," explains Prof. Henke.

The new findings show that scientists can exert much greater control over this process.

Metal-organic frameworks are materials built from metal centers connected by organic compounds. By introducing phenanthroline while these materials are molten, researchers can change the chemical connections within the structure before the glass solidifies.

"The crucial point is that the molecule does not simply remain as a filler," Prof. Henke continues. "It enters into a reaction. So we are altering the chemistry at precisely the moment when the material is still liquid."

stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
papers.authors: Stephen J. DeVience, John W. Blanchard, Camille G. McDonnell et al.
papers.tldr: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins.
takeaways: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields.

Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors.

We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T$_1$, T$_2$, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-$^{13}$C and a methanol-$^{13}$C/acetonitrile-2-$^{13}$C mixture at sample volumes $\sim$50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of $^1J_\text{CH}$ couplings and resolution between species.

papers.title: Recoverability of Gravitational Entanglement under Decoherence
papers.authors: Yi-Xuan Wang, Julen S. Pedernales, Martin B. Plenio
papers.tldr: Decoherence can make gravitationally generated entanglement arbitrarily small, or even vanishing, without necessarily rendering the effective matter dynamics separable. We ask whether this hidden non-separability can be revealed using strictly local quantum error correction.
takeaways: Decoherence can make gravitationally generated entanglement arbitrarily small, or even vanishing, without necessarily rendering the effective matter dynamics separable.

For GRW- and CSL-type noise, we analytically establish that strictly local quantum error correction can make the ratio of the effective gravitational interaction strength to the residual decoherence rate arbitrarily large for any parametrization of the collapse model, even in regimes where the unencoded entanglement signal approaches zero.
These results show that the loss of detectable entanglement is not equivalent to the loss of a recoverable non-separable resource, and open a route toward practical recovery protocols.

papers.title: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Based on PAS-Q
papers.authors: Yifan Wang, Li Xing, Ruigang Wang et al.
papers.tldr: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have attracted considerable attention for micro- and nanoscale thermometry owing to their high precision and spatial resolution. However, achieving sufficient electron spin polarization and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) typically requires high-power or long-duration laser excitation, which introduces heating and degrades measurement accuracy and stability.
takeaways: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have attracted considerable attention for micro- and nanoscale thermometry owing to their high precision and spatial resolution.

However, achieving sufficient electron spin polarization and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) typically requires high-power or long-duration laser excitation, which introduces heating and degrades measurement accuracy and stability.

This approach enables efficient spin polarization with reduced laser heating and improved optimization efficiency, and may be extended to other heat-sensitive quantum spin sensors, including silicon-vacancy centers in diamond and divacancy defects in silicon carbide.

papers.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
papers.authors: Chengyuan Cai, Hanchen Wang, Rui-Chun Xiao et al.
papers.tldr: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}.
takeaways: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting.

Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}.

When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents.

papers.title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
papers.authors: Jiyang Fan, Dinghui Wang, Tongshuai Zhu
papers.tldr: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons.
takeaways: Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate.
We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands.
